title: Ines and the Inheritance
premise: When the coffin of town founder Elias Marchetti is exhumed for a cemetery relocation, coroner Odile Oyelaran finds it empty — and a fresh body buried beneath it, a woman no one in town will admit to knowing. As Odile follows the dead woman's trail through twenty years of doctored records she herself once filed, she realizes the killer is someone who has been quietly editing the town's history alongside her, someone she trusts. In the end, Odile lures the killer into confessing at the tideline where the founder's remains were first hidden, choosing to expose the truth over protecting the found family that raised her — and the town, finally unburdened, gives its unknown woman a name and a grave.
about_author: August Almeida is the pen name of a former coastal-town archivist who spent a decade cataloguing municipal death records before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about small places that keep large secrets, drawn from the ledgers they were never supposed to read twice.

chapters.title: The Empty Box
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. During the founder's exhumation, Odile opens a coffin that should hold Elias Marchetti and finds only river stones — and beneath it, the body of an unidentified woman with her records number written on her palm. The town fathers urge discretion; Odile refuses. Emotional beat: her lifelong pride in knowing every grave curdles into the realization that one grave has been lying to her for decades.

chapters.title: Alphabet of the Dead
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, with flashbacks to her first year as coroner. Rechecking her own archived files, she finds pages subtly altered — dates shifted, names misspelled — in her own handwriting, or something close to it. She narrows the forger to the handful of people with file access: her deputy, the town clerk, and her old mentor, Father Anselm. Emotional beat: the horror of distrusting the records that made her feel she belonged.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The dead woman is identified as Marchetti's housekeeper, who vanished in 1979 — the same year the founder supposedly died at sea. When Odile confronts Anselm, he admits the town buried the founder's crimes, not his body, and begs her to let the sea keep its secret. That night her office is ransacked and her evidence file vanishes. Emotional beat: loyalty versus truth, and the discovery that her found family built its warmth on a buried woman.

chapters.title: A Name for the Grave
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, climax at the tideline. Feigning that the housekeeper's remains are being moved at dawn, Odile waits at the shore; the clerk — the true forger and the founder's illegitimate daughter — comes to destroy the last proof and confesses to the murder that protected her father's name. Odile records it all, then chooses arrest over cover-up. Emotional beat: the town buries the housekeeper under her own name at last, and Odile, no longer keeper of secrets, finally belongs to something honest.
